claim: The existing concrete Cl(5,5) TKK commutator and its modular grade-reversing action can be supplied as inhabitants of the repository's existing selected-law FiveGrading and GradeReversal structures on EndV, with the grade submodules tkkGrade (-2), tkkGrade (-1), tkkGrade 0, tkkGrade 1, and tkkGrade 2. The packaging preserves those exact carriers and does not claim a full indexed Lie-color structure or construct a categorical colimit.

operations: real-linear structure and associative endomorphism composition on EndV
tkkBracket X Y := X * Y - Y * X
tkkGrade k := eigenspace of tkkAdjointLinear at real eigenvalue k
conventions: The five labels are ordered -2, -1, 0, 1, 2 and indexed by Fin 5 via i ↦ i.val - 2.

The target FiveGrading interface records its five submodules, nested-product coordinate equivalence, sum reconstruction, and seven selected bracket laws; it is not a complete indexed graded-Lie interface.
Grade reversal means the supplied linear action sends each named grade to its opposite and preserves the bracket; involutivity remains a separately proved concrete property.

smallest_gap.pantograph_expression: Construct the FiveGrading on EndV using a local LieRing EndV := LieRing.ofAssociativeRing and LieAlgebra ℝ EndV := LieAlgebra.ofAssociativeAlgebra, explicitly identifying its bracket notation with tkkBracket. Set the five submodules to tkkGrade (-2), (-1), 0, 1, 2. Build the nested-product coordinate equivalence by composing the existing tkkFiveGradeDirectSumEquiv.symm, DirectSum.linearEquivFunOnFintype, and a proved Fin 5 Pi-to-nested-product linear equivalence; prove reconstruction is the ordered sum. Derive the seven selected bracket fields from tkk_bracket_grade_add and outside-range grade vanishing. Then package idealModularConjugationAction as GradeReversal using the existing grade-negation and bracket-preservation theorems. This is only an adapter; no new TKK closure or colimit theorem.
smallest_gap.description: The definitions must use the existing EndV, tkkBracket, tkkGrade, direct-sum equivalence, and modular conjugation. The nested-product coordinate equivalence is only a repackaging of the existing unique five-component decomposition. The generic GradeReversal target does not assert involutivity; if a direct-sum comparison is included, it must be stated as an explicit intertwining equality. The adapter must declare local associative-endomorphism Lie instances and show that their commutator is exactly the owner tkkBracket; coordinate equivalence must be constructed explicitly from the internal direct-sum equivalence rather than inferred from an existential decomposition theorem.
